title: Efficient Appliances: What to Know and What They Pay
desc: What to check before you buy an efficient appliance, and the appliance rebates we track, with the official page and the date we checked each one.
lead: Heat pump dryers, induction cooktops and efficient fridges can earn rebates. Here is what to check, and what pays today.
image_alt: A modern kitchen with light wood countertops and an island
intro:
Appliance rebates are small, but they add up when you replace several items. Programs tend to favour products that use less electricity, such as heat pump dryers, induction cooktops and efficient fridges and washers.

Most appliance rebates have the same three rules. The product must be on a list, usually ENERGY STAR or a higher tier. It often has to replace an existing appliance of a certain type. And you usually have to claim within a set time after you buy, with the receipt. The amounts we show are the range each program pays, since they differ by appliance.
checks: The right tier. Some programs pay only for the top efficiency tier, not for any ENERGY STAR product.
What you replace. Some pay only when an electric or gas appliance is swapped for an efficient one.
New, not used. Used and refurbished units are usually excluded.
Claim window. Many programs ask for the receipt within a set number of days. Put the date on your calendar.
Your utility. Some rebates depend on who sends your power bill.
faq: Is an induction cooktop worth it?
Many people like them for speed and cleaner indoor air. Whether the rebate covers the cost depends on your program.
For most appliances no. Gas appliances being replaced by electric ones may need an electrician.
Can I claim more than one appliance?
Often yes, up to the program's limit. The program page lists the amounts for each appliance.
Pick your province or state in the rebate finder to see what is open where you live.
extra:
Do the big things first

Appliance rebates are the smallest on this site, so do the larger upgrades first if you are planning several. Insulation and heating usually decide your bill. Replace appliances when they wear out, and check the program before you shop, so the model on your receipt is the model on the list.

Keep the receipt and the model number. Photograph the old appliance and the nameplate on the new one before it is installed. Programs sometimes ask for both.
